# Dataset Documentation

**File:** `ml-service/data/claims.csv` (regenerated by `ml-service/data/generate_dataset.py`)
**Size:** 9,000 claims · 160 providers · 1,099 members · 47 columns
**Fraud prevalence:** 10.3% (928 claims)
**RNG seed:** 20240517 (fully reproducible)

> ⚠️ **All data is synthetic.** No real patient, member, provider or claim information is used.
> Names are generated from common Indian first/last name lists; IDs are sequential.

---

## 1. Why simulate a payer ledger?

Public healthcare fraud datasets are scarce: they are either tiny, heavily de-identified to the point
of being unusable for feature engineering, or locked behind data-use agreements (e.g. CMS research
files). A final-year project therefore needs a **defensible simulation** — one that reproduces the
*statistical structure* that makes fraud detection hard, rather than a toy dataset with an obvious
answer.

This generator was written to satisfy four properties:

1. **Label provenance** — the fraud label is the *generating archetype*, not a rule, so ground truth
   is exact with zero privacy cost.
2. **Realistic imbalance** — ~10% prevalence: low enough to punish accuracy-based evaluation, high
   enough to train on.
3. **Partial observability** — a fraudulent claim trips only a subset of its usual red flags.
4. **Overlap with legitimate claims** — honest data is noisy, so no single feature is a giveaway.

## 2. Entities

### Providers (160)
Specialty drives the cost benchmark and the diagnosis vocabulary:

| Specialty | Benchmark cost | Specialty | Benchmark cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oncology | ₹1,50,000 | Radiology | ₹12,000 |
| Orthopedics | ₹1,20,000 | Dentistry | ₹9,000 |
| Cardiology | ₹95,000 | Dermatology | ₹8,000 |
| Neurology | ₹60,000 | Pharmacy | ₹6,000 |
| Gastroenterology | ₹45,000 | Pathology | ₹4,000 |

Attributes: licence age (N(11, 6) years), in-network flag (~78% in-network), prior fraud findings
(0 with 70% probability, 1 with 20%, 2 with 10%), peer-average billed amount (benchmark × N(0.98, 0.16)).

### Members (1,099)
Age ~ N(42, 17) truncated to [1, 92]; chronic conditions ~ Poisson depending on age band
(0.35 under 40, 1.6 at 40–64, 2.6 at 65+); five plan types; policy age ~ Exp(48) months;
premium by plan type.

### Claims (9,000)
Service dates span **2025-06-01 → 2026-03-27** (6329 claims in 2025, 2671 in 2026), with submission
dates falling 0–45 days after service. The generator derives the date window from `base_date` and its
seed, so regenerating with the same seed reproduces the same calendar exactly.

Claim IDs are derived from the **service date's** year, not `base_date`'s, so a claim submitted in
January 2026 for a December 2025 service is `CLM-2025-*`. (Using `base_date.year` produced IDs whose
year contradicted the claim's own date, and silently shifted every downstream case number.)

Claim type is drawn first, then refined by specialty (a Pharmacy provider bills pharmacy claims 75%
of the time, etc.).

## 3. The fraud archetypes

Weight mass is ~4.6% at the base rate, scaled by a risk lift (up to ×6 for a known ring member
transacting with a ring member), which lands overall prevalence near 10%.

| # | Archetype | Distortions applied |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `upcoding` | billed ×N(2.0, 0.75); units up; diagnosis–procedure match reduced by N(0.28, 0.16) |
| 2 | `phantom_billing` | billed ×N(2.4, 1.1); units ~N(11, 6.5); procedures ~N(5.5, 3.2); approval ratio ↑; late submission |
| 3 | `duplicate_billing` | duplicate similarity ~N(0.90, 0.09) (72% of the time); same-day claims up |
| 4 | `unbundling` | procedures ~N(9, 4.5); units ↑; billed ×N(1.75, 0.7) |
| 5 | `los_inflation` | service days ~N(13, 6.5); nights = days − 1; billed ×N(1.7, 0.7); **severity pushed down** |
| 6 | `collusion_ring` | billed ×N(2.0, 0.85); same-day claims ~N(3.4, 2.4); distance ~N(190, 140) km |
| 7 | `identity_misuse` | age-service mismatch (65% of the time); billed ×N(1.6, 0.7) |

### Severity
Every fraudulent claim draws `severity ~ Beta(1.7, 2.5)` clipped to [0.10, 1.0]; distorted fields are
interpolated linearly between the honest baseline and the full-strength scheme:

```
value = legit + (fraud - legit) * severity
```

### Signal dropout
Each distorted signal is independently withheld with probability 0.30 (0.40 for procedures and
diagnosis–procedure match, 0.50 for duplicate similarity, same-day claims and age mismatch).
A fraud claim therefore carries **partial** evidence, and different claims of the same scheme look
different.

### Benign data-quality noise (legitimate claims)
| Noise | Rate / distribution |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis–procedure coding drift | 5% of claims, match ~N(0.60, 0.12) |
| Honest resubmission | 4.5% of claims, duplicate similarity ~N(0.78, 0.09) |
| Age-service mismatch (data entry) | 3% of claims |
| Baseline duplicate similarity | Exp(0.055) |
| Submission lag | N(4, 2.5) days clipped to [0, 45] |
| Distance | LogN(2.6, 0.9) km |

| Column | Type | Description |

| `claim_id` | string | `CLM-<year>-<seq>` |

| `provider_license_age_years` | float | practice age |
| `provider_fraud_history` | int | prior adverse findings |
| `provider_in_network` | 0/1 | network status |

| `units_claimed`, `service_days`, `nights_in_hospital`, `num_procedures` | int | utilisation |
| `prior_claims_30d`, `member_claims_12m`, `provider_claims_30d`, `same_day_claims` | int | frequency signals |
| `duplicate_similarity` | 0–1 | similarity to a prior claim |
| `diag_proc_match` | 0–1 | clinical consistency of the coding |
| `age_service_mismatch` | 0/1 | procedure implausible for member age |
| `submission_lag_days`, `is_weekend_submission` | int | process signals |
| `distance_km` | float | member residence → provider |

| `specialty_amount_mean`, `specialty_amount_std` | ₹ | specialty benchmark statistics |
| **`archetype`** | string | **ground-truth scheme** |
| **`is_fraud`** | 0/1 | **ground-truth label** |
| **`fraud_severity`** | 0–1 | **ground-truth severity** (0 for legitimate) |

## 5. Derived features (32)

Computed identically in `ml-service/features.py` and `server/src/services/featureService.js`.
Grouped by what they measure:

**Monetary (6)** — `amount_billed` (log1p), `approved_ratio`, `billed_vs_peer_ratio`,
`amount_zscore_specialty`, `procedure_avg_cost_ratio` (vs specialty benchmark), `units_claimed`.

**Utilisation (8)** — `service_days`, `nights_in_hospital`, `los_expected_ratio` (vs expected LOS per
claim type), `num_procedures`, `prior_claims_30d_member`, `member_claim_frequency_12m`,
`provider_claims_30d`, `same_day_multiple_claims`.

**Integrity (4)** — `duplicate_similarity`, `diag_proc_match`, `age_service_mismatch`,
`diagnosis_severity_score`.

**Temporal (2)** — `submission_lag_days`, `is_weekend_submission`.

**Provider / network (5)** — `provider_specialty_risk` (documented prior), `provider_license_age_years`,
`provider_fraud_history`, `provider_network_status`, `distance_member_provider_km`.

**Member / policy (4)** — `member_age`, `member_chronic_conditions`, `policy_age_months`,
`premium_to_billed_ratio`.

**Categorical encodings (3)** — `claim_type_risk`, `is_emergency`, `pharmacy_qty_ratio`.

## 6. Observed signal strength

Single-feature ROC-AUC on the full dataset (0.5 = no signal, 1.0 = deterministic):

| Feature | ROC-AUC | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `approved_ratio` | 0.774 | Strongest single signal — fraudsters approve their own inflated bills |
| `member_claim_frequency_12m` | 0.741 | Ring churn |
| `units_claimed` | 0.722 | Phantom billing / unbundling |
| `provider_claims_30d` | 0.711 | Provider volume |
| `billed_vs_peer_ratio` | 0.706 | Upcoding |
| `procedure_avg_cost_ratio` | 0.702 | Upcoding |
| `same_day_multiple_claims` | 0.674 | Duplicate / ring |
| `distance_member_provider_km` | 0.661 | Ring geography |

No single feature exceeds 0.8 — the intended difficulty bar. A model must combine evidence.

## 7. Reproducing / modifying

```bash
cd ml-service
python data/generate_dataset.py --rows 9000 --providers 160 --members 1100 \
       --out data/claims.csv --json data/claims_seed.json

python train_models.py --data data/claims.csv --out models
```

To experiment: change `ARCHETYPE_WEIGHTS` (prevalence), the `Beta` parameters in `sev`
(severity distribution), or the `keep()` probabilities (observability). Re-run training and note how
PR-AUC moves — that sensitivity analysis is a strong addition to the report.

## 8. Known limitations

* No temporal drift, seasonality or policy changes over the period.
* Providers are static (no ownership changes, no group-practice structures).
* No clinical free text, prior-authorisation records or pharmacy–prescriber linkage — the features
  that would catch subtle upcoding in reality.
* Fraud archetypes are drawn independently; real rings co-occur with other schemes.
